title: Messaging MMS Received Event
description: An inbound MMS text reached one of the operator's lines. Producers: the Telnyx messaging webhook. Consumers deduplicate on message_id: the same text can be observed twice (SMS broadcast and its notification). One entity per transport (messaging.<transport>.<action>), the same split as the chat platforms; carrier texts order per operator line, ordering_key line:<line>, so one conversation stays ordered when it switches SMS/MMS or falls back from RCS. Calls and voicemail stay in telephony. See bloodbank/docs/event-naming.md (messaging).

ordering_key.description: Section 11.1 bucket 'line:<line>', the same value as 'line:' + data.line: every carrier text on one operator line orders together, whatever the transport.

message_id.description: Stable id: the provider message id, or <source>:<source event id>.

line.description: The operator line involved: 'cell' (the personal Verizon line, forwarded from the Android phone), 'imessage' (the operator's iMessage account on the Mac, through BlueBubbles), or the E.164 of a Telnyx number.

source_app.description: Android package that showed the notification (android-notification only), e.g. com.google.android.apps.messaging.

from.description: E.164 number such as +12155550100, or the sender's display name when the source exposes only that (RCS/iMessage notifications).

from_name.description: Contact or business display name, when known.

to.description: E.164 of the receiving number, or the line label.

text.description: Message body as observed. Notifications may truncate long bodies.

url.description: Fetchable URL; provider URLs can expire.

received_at.description: When the line received it (source clock).

verification_code.description: A one-time code the producer extracted, when the text is a verification message.

thread_id.description: Conversation identifier at the source, when it has one.
